non_authority: Canonical relations are context and retrieval-risk evidence only; they do not authorize boundaries.
Later reuse does not establish identity, fulfillment, theology, law, authorship, chronology, or witness preference.
WEB coordinates govern coverage; OSHB and UXLC are correlated WLC-family corroborations, not independent witnesses.
WEB Mal.4.1-4.6 to MT/WLC Mal.3.19-3.24 is versification metadata only.
All units are candidate-only and non-authorizing.

versification.crosswalk: WEB Mal.4.1-4.6 maps to OSHB/UXLC Mal.3.19-3.24.

route.title: Burden heading and love-of-Jacob disputation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The massa/word/by-Malachi heading is taken up by 'I have loved you,' the quoted 'How?' objection, the Jacob-Edom comparison, and the recognition close at 1:5; the son-and-servant analogy with direct priestly address at 1:6 starts a new dispute.
route.rationale: Keep the heading with the complete claim-objection-evidence-result exchange. Edom's counterclaim at 1:4 and the audience's recognition at 1:5 prevent 1:2-3 from becoming a decontextualized Jacob/Esau maxim.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.1.1 alone was rejected because it has no independent literary action and invites messenger-name speculation.
Mal.1.2-1.3 alone was rejected because Edom's counterclaim and the recognition coda complete the dispute.
route.counterevidence: WEB places a paragraph before 1:2, permitting title display as metadata but not an unhydrated literary surface.
route.proof_text_guard: Retrieve Jacob/Esau with the love claim, objection, Edom counterclaim, and 1:5 close; encode no election, ethnicity, identity, or fulfillment conclusion.

canonical_relations.relation: Earlier Jacob/Esau and Edom narrative context
canonical_relations.guard: Background does not decide Malachi's boundary or love/hate scope.
Thematic proximity is not authorship or chronology evidence.
Romans cannot carve the quotation out of Malachi's local dispute.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: Retrieval surfaces only 1:2-3 and lets Romans erase Edom's objection and the recognition close.
premortem_failure.impact: The local dispute becomes an identity or election slogan.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Surface 1:1-5 and expose later relations only as guarded metadata.

route.title: Priests, polluted offerings, and great-King close
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Mal.1.6 names the priests and launches repeated 'How?' objections; 1:14 closes the offering panels with curse, great-King declaration, and feared-name refrain before 'Now ... this command' restarts at 2:1.
route.rationale: Honor accusation, polluted table, defective animals, governor comparison, rejected altar, nations contrast, renewed accusation, curse, and kingship result form one dispute. This prevents 1:11 from becoming an isolated ritual proof text.
rejected_alternatives: The 1:6-9 | 1:10-14 split was rejected because the latter repeats table, offering, name, and acceptance and supplies the conclusion.
Mal.1.11 alone was rejected because later ritual readings are reception questions, not a seam.
Mal.1.14 alone was rejected because its curse is the dispute's result.
route.counterevidence: WEB paragraphs at 1:9, 1:10, and 1:14 plus the WLC-family samekh after MT 1:13 mark dependent movements, but 1:14 completes the curse and royal result.

internal_seams.treatment: appeal to altar-rejection and nations contrast
source paragraph retained, but 1:14 hydrates backward as the close

route.proof_text_guard: Do not surface 1:11, 1:13, or 1:14 without the polluted-offering dispute; tense, ritual referent, and later worship claims remain unresolved.

canonical_relations.relation: Torah restrictions on defective sacrificial animals
canonical_relations.guard: The relation explains the accusation but decides no present law or priestly legitimacy.
Resemblance does not authorize detaching 1:11.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: Mal.1.11 is isolated to settle offering tense, identity, or ritual fulfillment.
premortem_failure.impact: Reception replaces the local priestly accusation as boundary authority.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Keep 1:6-14 whole, tag 1:11 as an internal hot zone, and hydrate to 1:6-2:9.

route.title: Command to priests and threatened curse
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: וְעַתָּה and 'this command is for you, priests' open at 2:1; 2:4 states recognition and covenant-of-Levi purpose, while 2:5 shifts to retrospective comparison, 'My covenant was with him.'
route.rationale: Expose command, conditional refusal, curse, bodily consequence, and purpose as a dependent child. The purpose in 2:4 explains the threat, whereas 2:5 begins the Levi ideal panel.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.2.1-2.3 was rejected because 2:4 gives purpose.
Mal.1.6-2.9 as the only surface was rejected because וְעַתָּה supports a dependent movement with mandatory hydration.
Mal.2.3 alone was rejected because offspring/seed and rebuke are translation hot zones.
route.counterevidence: The covenant-purpose clause in 2:4 points forward, so 2:1-9 remains a mandatory parent.
route.proof_text_guard: Curse, blessing, offspring/seed, or rebuke retrieval must hydrate 2:1-9 and disclose 2:3 translation pressure.

canonical_relations.guard: Context does not identify Mal.2.2's blessings or authorize a present curse.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: Mal.2.2-3 is retrieved as a curse formula or its seed wording treated as settled genealogy.
premortem_failure.impact: Translation pressure and covenant purpose disappear.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Keep 2:1-4 intact, require 2:1-9 hydration, and preserve lexical uncertainty.

route.title: Levi ideal, present failure, and public verdict
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: 'My covenant was with him' opens Levi's ideal at 2:5; 'But you have turned aside' reverses the panel at 2:8, and 2:9 closes with public consequence and a pe before the communal questions at 2:10.
route.rationale: Keep ideal, present contrast, and verdict together so 'messenger of Yahweh' at 2:7 remains a role inside this comparison, surfaced only under the 2:1-9 parent.
rejected_alternatives: The 2:5-7 | 2:8-9 split was rejected because the accusation depends on the ideal.
Mal.2.7 alone was rejected because messenger language describes priestly knowledge within the comparison.
One 2:1-9 surface was rejected only for retrieval granularity; its parent status remains mandatory.
route.counterevidence: Mal.2.5 can continue 2:4's purpose clause, which is why the parent cannot be optional.
route.proof_text_guard: Do not retrieve 2:7 as a universal office definition or identify its messenger with 3:1; hydrate ideal, failure, verdict, and command parent.

canonical_relations.guard: The relation settles no succession, office, or legal authority.
It does not make Malachi an exhaustive office definition.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: Mal.2.7 becomes a stand-alone office definition or a later messenger identity.

route.title: Communal father-and-covenant treachery accusation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: First-person-plural questions about one father, creator, brotherhood, and covenant restart at 2:10; Judah's accusation and cut-off consequence close at the pe after 2:12 before 'This again/secondly' at 2:13.
route.rationale: Treat 2:10-12 as the first dependent treachery panel. Its communal questions, foreign-god idiom, and consequence cohere, while 2:13 explicitly introduces a second panel.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.2.10 alone was rejected because its questions introduce the accusation.
Mal.2.11-12 alone was rejected because 2:10 governs them.
Mal.2.10-16 as the only surface was rejected because pe plus וְזֹאת שֵׁנִית supports dependent children under one parent.
route.counterevidence: Repeated treachery language links 2:10-12 to 2:13-16, so neither child can be an independent law.
route.proof_text_guard: Foreign-god and marriage wording must not become ethnic, racial, marital, or exclusion policy; preserve referent uncertainty and parent hydration.

canonical_relations.guard: Relations settle no ethnicity or present law.
Subject overlap proves no date, dependence, or identical circumstance.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: The foreign-god phrase is operationalized as ethnic or marital policy.
premortem_failure.impact: A local accusation becomes unauthorized identity law.

route.title: Altar tears and wife-of-youth treachery
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: 'This again/secondly' opens at 2:13; the quoted 'Why?' receives the wife-of-youth covenant answer, and repeated guard-your-spirit exhortation plus samekh closes at 2:16 before the justice complaint.
route.rationale: Keep tears, rejected offering, objection, witness, wife covenant, compressed one/Spirit/offspring syntax, hate/divorce/garment/violence wording, and repeated treachery warning together. Difficulty requires context, not micro-units.
rejected_alternatives: The 2:13-14 | 2:15-16 split was rejected because the answer continues through the closing exhortation.
Mal.2.15 or 2:16 alone was rejected because each has severe translation pressure.
The 2:10-16 parent remains mandatory despite a real second-panel onset.
route.counterevidence: Compressed Hebrew in 2:15-16 leaves clause relations contested; confidence concerns onset and close, not a selected translation.

internal_seams.treatment: translation hot zone inside the answer

route.proof_text_guard: No marriage, divorce, Spirit, offspring, hate, violence, or gender rule may be inferred; include 2:13-16, its parent, and translation uncertainty.

canonical_relations.guard: Relations do not solve 2:15-16 syntax or authorize divorce law.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: A translation of 2:15 or 2:16 is silently selected as complete marriage doctrine.
premortem_failure.impact: Textual compression and the altar dispute disappear.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Keep four verses together, hydrate the parent, and label alternatives without choosing.

route.title: Justice complaint answered by messenger, refiner, and witness
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Mal.2.17 asks 'Where is the God of justice?'; 3:1 answers 'Behold, I send my messenger,' 3:2-4 develops refining and restored offering, and 3:5 resolves the complaint with a swift judgment witness. Mal.3.6 starts the return dispute.
route.rationale: Preserve this cross-chapter question-answer unit. Neither messenger expression, the refiner image, nor the social-judgment list should be detached from complaint and answer.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.2.17 alone was rejected because 3:1-5 answers it.
Mal.3.1 alone was rejected because messenger identity and later quotation are reception questions.
Mal.3.1-4 | 3:5 was rejected because the witness supplies the judicial resolution.
route.counterevidence: WEB's chapter edge and paragraph before 3:5 support internal retrieval only; the justice frame is stronger.

internal_seams.treatment: chapter seam rejected; complaint and answer joined
judgment witness retained as answer result

route.proof_text_guard: Retrieve 3:1 with 2:17-3:5; do not identify messengers, select fulfillment, conflate 2:7 with 3:1, or let Gospel reuse authorize a boundary.

canonical_relations.guard: Relations do not prove identical referents.
Later use cannot detach 3:1 or settle fulfillment.
Context does not reduce the oracle to a checklist.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: Mal.3.1 is isolated, a messenger identified, and Gospel reuse made boundary authority.
premortem_failure.impact: The justice dispute becomes an identity proof text.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Make 2:17-3:5 the surface and guard all later relations.

route.title: Return, robbery, tithe remedy, and blessing
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The unchanging claim and return summons at 3:6-7 provoke 'How shall we return?', answered by robbery at 3:8, then curse, remedy, test, crop protection, and nations coda close at the samekh after 3:12.
route.rationale: Keep return frame, accusation, tithes answer, remedy, test, blessing, agricultural protection, and public result together. Splitting 3:7/8 separates objection from answer and makes 3:10 transactional.
rejected_alternatives: The 3:6-7 | 3:8-12 split was rejected because 3:8 answers 3:7.
Mal.3.10 alone was rejected because it depends on accusation, remedy, crop result, and nations coda.
Mal.3.8-10 was rejected because 3:11-12 complete the outcome.
route.counterevidence: WEB's paragraph before 3:8 supports an internal seam, not an unhydrated surface.
route.proof_text_guard: Never surface 3:10 without 3:6-12. Torah tithe relations authorize no modern levy, prosperity transaction, storehouse identity, or financial promise.

canonical_relations.guard: Relations settle no present law or institutional identity.
Similarity proves no chronology or identical circumstance.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: Mal.3.10 is returned alone as guaranteed financial return or institutional authority.
premortem_failure.impact: Return accusation and agricultural-public outcome vanish.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Surface 3:6-12 and guard Torah/Nehemiah links as context only.

route.title: Service protest and fearers' counter-scene
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Harsh words and 'What have we spoken?' lead through the no-profit protest in 3:13-15; 'Then those who feared' opens the answering counter-scene, whose memory record, possession promise, and discernment close at 3:18 with samekh.
route.rationale: Keep protest and counter-scene together so the fearers function as the answer to claims that service is vain and the wicked prosper. The samekh supports a dependent day-oracle next, but both children require 3:13-4:3.
rejected_alternatives: The 3:13-15 | 3:16-18 split was rejected because the fearers answer the protest.
Mal.3.16-17 alone was rejected because 3:18 completes discernment.
One 3:13-4:3 surface was rejected only because samekh plus כי הנה supports a dependent day child.
route.counterevidence: WEB's paragraph before 3:16 and speaker shift mark a strong internal seam, but answer function prevents standalone use.
route.proof_text_guard: Book-of-memory and possession language stays inside the protest answer and cannot become a salvation registry, identity test, or merit doctrine.

canonical_relations.guard: Shared imagery proves no identical register, persons, or soteriology.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: Mal.3.16-17 becomes an individual membership registry detached from protest and discernment.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Surface 3:13-18 and hydrate to 3:13-4:3 for day language.

route.title: Coming day: burning and healing contrast
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: WEB 4:1/MT 3:19 opens כי הנה, 'For behold, the day comes'; burning of the proud contrasts with 'But to you who fear my name' at 4:2 and closes with ashes at 4:3, followed by pe and 'Remember' at 4:4.
route.rationale: The oracle has onset, contrast, and source close, permitting a dependent child. Yet causal 'For' answers 3:13-18's protest and discernment, so standalone presentation remains contested and parent hydration is mandatory.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.4.1 or 4:2 alone was rejected because judgment and healing contrast completes at 4:3.
One 3:13-4:3 surface remains nearly equal, but samekh, כי הנה, and pe support a dependent child.
Mal.4.1-3 without parent hydration was rejected because 'For' makes it the prior movement's outcome.
route.counterevidence: Causal כי and repeated proud/wicked, fear/name, serving, and day language bind the oracle to 3:13-18.
route.hold_question: Should Mal.4.1-4.3 be independently surfaced with mandatory hydration to Mal.3.13-4.3, or remain an internal day-oracle seam because כי הנה supplies the reasoned answer to Mal.3.13-18?
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate furnace, sun, healing, or trampling imagery to make a timetable, identify a figure, or authorize violence; require 3:13-4:3 hydration.

canonical_relations.guard: Shared imagery does not synchronize timelines, identify actors, or decide boundaries.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: The day oracle becomes a timeline, sun-identity claim, or warrant against a labeled group.
premortem_failure.impact: Rhetorical contrast becomes eschatological or social authority.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Hold presentation treatment, mandate 3:13-4:3, and leave images unresolved.

route.title: Remember Moses and send Elijah coda
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: After pe, 4:4 commands 'Remember the law of Moses ... at Horeb'; 4:5 begins 'Behold, I will send you Elijah,' and 4:6 gives kinship-turning purpose plus the lest-I-strike-with-herem close.
route.rationale: Preserve the paired remembrance-and-sending coda. The commands form internal panels, but Moses/Horeb, Elijah sending, reconciliation purpose, and curse risk jointly govern final retrieval.
rejected_alternatives: The 4:4 | 4:5-6 split was rejected because they form a paired Torah-and-prophet coda.
Mal.4.5-6 alone was rejected because later reuse can erase the Moses frame.
Mal.4.6 alone was rejected because herem is the coda's consequence, not a standalone curse.
route.counterevidence: WEB paragraphs before 4:4 and 4:5 and the imperative-to-future shift support two dependent internal panels.

internal_seams.treatment: two panels retained, neither surfaced independently

route.proof_text_guard: Do not use Gospel reuse to identify Elijah, decide fulfillment, or detach 4:5-6 from Moses/Horeb; never surface herem alone.

canonical_relations.guard: Context does not make the coda a complete legal corpus.
Background does not settle the promised referent or manner.

canonical_relations.relation: Later reuse of Elijah and kinship-turning language
canonical_relations.guard: Later interpretation is never identity, fulfillment, or boundary authority.

premortem_failure.failure_mode: Mal.4.5-6 is isolated and Gospel reuse settles Elijah identity while Moses and the curse-risk syntax vanish.
premortem_failure.impact: The paired coda becomes an identity proof text.
premortem_failure.mitigation: Surface 4:4-6 whole and attach non-identity/non-fulfillment guards.

Mal.1.11 can become a tense or ritual proof text.
Mal.2.15-16 pressure can be hidden beneath marriage law.
Mal.3.1 can become a messenger-identity proof text.
Mal.3.10 can become a prosperity or institutional formula.
Mal.4.1-3 has a strong dependent seam but remains causally tied to Mal.3.13-18.
